The new green rate for the Belgian franc came into force on Thursday whilst the Irish green rate started its first confirmation period of a possible five. On the basis of exchange rates on 21 November, the RMG for the Irish punt is greater than +5 percent and is therefore currently forecast to enter its second confirmation period on 1 December.

Any currencies with negative RMGs for the period will devalue on 1 December by reducing their negative gaps to zero. Therefore, devaluations are currently forecast for the Belgian franc, the Dutch florin, the German mark and the Austrian schilling on 1 December.

Since the average RMG for sterling is also greater than +5 percent, and any revaluation of the UK green rate would be appreciable, it is currently forecast to enter the first of a possible five confirmation periods on 1 December prior to a potential revaluation on 21 January. During confirmation periods the three-day (six percent) rule is suspended.
